subject: Re: Multipliers or multiplying transect length?

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: Multipliers or multiplying transect length?
parts:
Delyth:

My opinion is that multiplying the line length by the number of visits
is a more accurate representation of what took place. The effort you
expended is measured in kilometres walked which is equal to line length
times number of transits of those lines.

Distance knows nothing about the identity of the individuals you
encountered. Repeated sightings of animals by walking the same transect
twice does not affect the point estimate of density. If you look at the
formula for estimating density you will see embedded inside it the ratio
(n/L) detections divided by effort. This is called the encounter rate.

Imagine you are trying to estimate density of trees in the desert and
there is only a single tree in the desert. You choose to only place one
transect in your desert of length 1km, and that transect happens to be
sufficiently close to the tree that you detect it from this transect.
If you walk the transect once (and detect your tree), the encounter rate
is 1/1km. If you walk the transect a second time (and detect the tree
again), the effort doubles to 2km, but the detections also double,
leaving the encounter rate at 2/2km=1/1km.

What is missing from this story is the variability of that encounter
rate. We would like to know how representative the places we visit is
of the entire desert. Well, by having but a single transect, we do not
know how variable this encounter rate is throughout the desert.
Likewise for your study, walking transects multiple times provides
little information about the spatial variability in encounter rate
through the study area for which you are drawing inference.
